conversations.title: Woman With Dwarfism Opens Up About Dating, and the Behavior She Can’t Ignore
conversations.reply: The 'downright creepy' behaviour she names is only the loud half of it. Disabled daters have flagged the quieter half for years: attentive and warm right up until dating her body becomes real, then a sudden disappearance with no explanation offered.

conversations.title: Parkinson’s drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone.
conversations.reply: A neurologist saying plainly that Parkinson's changes sex lives shouldn't be rare, yet it is. Chronically ill and disabled people have described this same gap for years: intimacy assumed to stop cold at diagnosis, with mainstream dating built to assume the same.

conversations.title: Time to Pay Attention: This Is Bigger Than Any One Policy
conversations.reply: Calling this 'bigger than any one policy' undersells it: disabled people have watched protections built over decades get unpicked one technicality at a time under polite committee language. The erosion isn't new, only the willingness to name it in public is.

conversations.title: People in Jersey asked to share their views on island life
conversations.reply: Asking disabled islanders for their experience is only useful if the answers change something, not just fill a filed report. Disabled people in Jersey, like everywhere else, have been giving these same answers about access for years with little to show for it.

conversations.title: Aurora proclamation of Disability Pride Month seen as part of efforts to better support residents with disabilities
conversations.reply: A council proclamation is a start, not a finish line. The real test of Disability Pride Month is whether that city's venues, transport and nightlife actually back it up that same weekend, not just its agenda paperwork.

target: Roll with Cole and Charisma (interabled couple)
target_reply: Cole and Charisma's relationship keeps getting flattened into either a feel-good story or something people quietly wonder is fetish, never simply two people who chose each other. Interabled couples have described this exact reflex.

instagram_hitlist.who: An interabled couple who post about their relationship (search for creators tagging content as interabled or mixed-ability couples)
instagram_hitlist.why: Their comment sections are a live demonstration of how strangers react to visible disability in a relationship
instagram_hitlist.comment: Every comment section under posts like this proves the point: strangers treat interabled couples as content before they treat them as a couple, and disabled daters have named that stare for years.

instagram_hitlist.who: #disabilitydating - look for a post venting about mainstream dating apps and being ghosted after disclosing a disability
instagram_hitlist.why: Direct, current example of the disclosure-then-silence pattern the app was built to challenge
instagram_hitlist.comment: Whoever wrote this under this tag has just described a Tuesday. Disabled daters have said for years that disclosure is the exact moment the messages stop, whatever the app's marketing claims.

instagram_hitlist.who: A Manchester-based accessibility or disability-led community account covering the city's venues and nightlife
instagram_hitlist.why: Direct fit with the core exclusion theme, especially anything touching the Gay Village or big nights out
instagram_hitlist.comment: Manchester loves calling itself a nightlife city, right up until someone asks which of those venues a wheelchair user can actually get into. Disabled residents have been flagging the same short list of accessible doors for years.

instagram_hitlist.who: #wheelchairlife - look for an access-fail post about a venue or event with steps and no step-free route
instagram_hitlist.why: Concrete, current example of the venue exclusion the account should always be pressing on
instagram_hitlist.comment: Another night out that only works if you can climb stairs to reach it. Wheelchair users have been posting this exact scene under this tag for years and the venues still act surprised.

instagram_hitlist.who: A disabled dating advocate or creator who shares personal dating experiences as a disabled person
instagram_hitlist.why: Reinforces the disclosure-and-disappear pattern with a recognisable, ongoing voice in the space
instagram_hitlist.comment: This is the account worth following for anyone who thinks disabled daters overstate what happens after disclosure. The stories keep matching because the behaviour keeps repeating.

instagram_hitlist.who: #accessibility - look for a genuine access win, such as step-free access or a ramp fitted at a venue
instagram_hitlist.why: A rare good-news post that deserves proper recognition, in line with the access-win celebration rule
instagram_hitlist.comment: More venues doing this, please. Step-free access fitted without a campaign first is what basic respect looks like, not a bonus feature to be grateful for.
